Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- github-morning-reporter: Use this agent when the user requests a morning report, daily summary, or overview of their GitHub activity. Trigger phrases include 'morning report', 'github report', 'daily github summary', 'what's happening on github', or 'check my github status'. This agent should be used proactively when the user starts their day or explicitly asks for repository updates.

Examples:
- User: "get me my morning github report"
  Assistant: "I'll use the github-morning-reporter agent to generate your comprehensive GitHub status report."
  <uses Agent tool to invoke github-morning-reporter>

- User: "what's new on my repos today?"
  Assistant: "Let me pull together your GitHub morning report using the github-morning-reporter agent."
  <uses Agent tool to invoke github-morning-reporter>

- User: "show me my daily github summary"
  Assistant: "I'll generate your daily GitHub summary using the github-morning-reporter agent."
  <uses Agent tool to invoke github-morning-reporter> (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qa-agent: A static pre-ship audit. Invoke it right before shipping, opening a PR, or merging — or when the user explicitly asks "does this pass QA?". It reads the diff and returns PASS or BLOCK with specific findings. It reviews and reports; it never edits code. Examples:

<example>

user: "ok ship it"
assistant: "Before shipping, let me run the qa-agent on the diff for a PASS/BLOCK verdict."
<commentary>Ship boundary — run the gate.</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly asks for a quality check.
user: "does this pass QA?"
assistant: "Running the qa-agent on the current diff."
<commentary>Direct request for the gate.</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

input.description: Extract alt card design spec
input.prompt:
You are a documentation-discovery agent. Extract complete, citation-backed facts about the "Session ALT lifecycle card" design from two files:

1. /Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro/design/timeline-cards/DESIGN-SPEC.md — especially section 6 "Session ALT card — lifecycle demo (lines 376–682)" (starts around line 427), but also skim the whole file's section map so you can report which OTHER sections describe the standard session card, observation rows/cards, rails/strip, and live session card (§7), since the alt card will replace/absorb some of those.
2. /Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro/design/timeline-cards/timeline-cards.dc.html — the design source. The alt card section is lines 376–682 (`<section id="sess-s1-alt">`). The runtime state machine lives in the JS near lines 2100–2250 (renderVals, _runAlt, _stopAlt, altGoToObs, onMagicKind, KINDSUM).

Report back with:

A. **Alt card DOM structure**, top to bottom, with dc.html line references: tinted head (altBg/altArc arc rings), head row (summary icon vs prompt label swap, "alt layout" tag, streaming counter, distilling indicator, settled state with Replay button and Summary/Prompt segmented control), the big h2/p title swap (summary headline vs quoted prompt), the collapsible summary body (Learned/Completed/Next-steps rows), the observation index/chips region (lines ~546+ mention obs-101258b etc. and altGoToObs), and the distill/magic panel (lines 522–556). Quote exact inline styles for the key containers (copy-ready).

B. **State machine**: every alt* state variable (altView, altPhase, altN, altMagic), their possible values, which renderVals entries they drive (altBg, altHeadBorder, altArc, altSumOp/altPromOp/altSumPe/altPromPe, altSumRows, altSumVis/altSumVisDelay, altPanelRows, altObsLabel, altSegSumBg etc.), and the exact _runAlt() timing sequence in milliseconds (what happens at each timeout: when does each observation land, when does distill start, when does it settle). Also _stopAlt() and altGoToObs() behavior — what exactly happens when you click an observation chip (which state flips, what the main card shows).

C. **How observations render inside the alt card** — the obs index rows/chips: their DOM, kind icons, titles, times, and whether facts/narrative appear anywhere in the alt design (expandable or not). Also the "magic"/KINDSUM distill-by-kind feature (onMagicKind): what it does.

D. **CSS tokens used** (--butter-100, --lilac-100, --line-1, etc.) and any keyframe animations referenced (dcPulse etc.), with where they're defined in dc.html.

E. **Contrast with the standard (non-alt) session card** (§ earlier in spec, around dc.html lines ~180–375) and the §7 Live Session Card spec: 3–5 bullets on what structurally differs, so the implementer knows what to remove/replace.

Format: use exact quotes for inline styles (they are copy-ready — this design uses inline styles, not classes). Include file:line citations for EVERYTHING. End with a Confidence note + known gaps.

input.prompt:
You are a documentation-discovery agent. Map the current timeline-viewer implementation in /Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro/src/components/timeline-viewer/ so an implementer can replace the current observation card with a new "alt card" design and rework the live-session animation cycle. Read the actual files; cite file:line for everything.

Report back on:

A. **ObsCard.tsx** — full current structure: props, DOM, what it renders (title, facts, narrative?), where it's instantiated (grep TimelineViewer.tsx / SessionCard.tsx), and which CSS classes in cards.css style it (list the class names and their line ranges in cards.css). Note: the design had 2 card variants and this one is being REPLACED by the alt design.

B. **SessionCard.tsx** — the live variant: all live-related props and state (data-live, tcv-hero--landed, playhead, lastStreamObs handling, wrap-to-summary lifecycle), timers, and how the Summary/Prompt toggle works today. Which parts are the "hero" (big title area) and how the summary body (Learned/Completed/Next-steps) renders.

C. **useRailSync.ts** — the full RailSyncApi: jumpToObs, landObs, flash/highlight mechanics (what CSS classes get toggled on rail dots/obs elements, e.g. flash classes), and how dot↔card hover/jump works. What would be needed to add a "bold border highlight" on a rail obs box and a "click rail item → swap main card to that observation" interaction.

D. **Strip.tsx and Ruler.tsx** — how rail obs boxes/dots are rendered (data attributes, ids like data-obs), the live "Now Watching" group, playhead (playFrac), and existing click handlers on rail items.

E. **TimelineViewer.tsx** — live session wiring: liveState/lastStreamObs prop flow, the streamed-obs landing effect, wrap handling, dayMeta "· recording", ask card state (just enough to not break it). Also how sessions/obs data flows from timeline-data.ts/types.ts (ObsItem/SessionItem shapes — quote the exact type definitions).

F. **fixture.ts + dev preview harness** — the live demo fixture (id='live', hasSummary=false, suffixed obs ids), the /dev/viewer-preview page path and its ?ask=1 / ?demo=live query modes, and how _runLive-equivalent demo timing is driven today (file:line). How would an implementer verify the new animation cycle with Playwright against this harness (what URL, what selectors exist today).

G. **cards.css inventory** — line ranges for: obs card styles, live session styles (Phase 4 additions), ask card styles — so the implementer knows what CSS to delete/replace vs keep.

H. **Sessions without summaries** — how a session with hasSummary=false renders today (both live and non-live). The user says summaries sometimes never arrive; the new design must degrade cleanly.

Format: concrete findings with exact names/signatures and file:line citations. Flag anything that looks like the OLD second card variant the user mentioned ("we did have 2 in there"). End with a Confidence note + known gaps.

types in `src/components/cloud-viewer/types.ts`. - `useSSE()` (`src/hooks/useSSE.ts:113`) → `{ observations, summaries, prompts, projects, isProcessing, isConnected }`. SSE `initial_load` carries **projects only** — history comes from `/api/observations|summaries|prompts` pagination. - `useStats()` (`src/hooks/useStats.ts`) → `{ stats }`; cloud payload is `{ observationCount, summaryCount, promptCount, projects }` (`src/app/api/stats/route.ts:18–23`). **No session count, no compression %** — sessions derive from `data.sessions.length`; there is no compression stat (see Phase 2 stat mapping). - Auth plumbing: `signOut` from `@/lib/auth-client` (used in old `HeaderControls.tsx:234`). - Deps available: `react` 19.2 / `next` ^16 (React Compiler ON), `lucide-react` ^1.17, `framer-motion` ^12 (avoid for this build — plain CSS animations match the design), Tailwind v4 present but the viewer is **plain CSS**. - Theme: `html[data-theme]` written pre-paint by `THEME_BOOT` (`src/app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx:14`, keys `cmem-theme` → legacy `theme` → system) and at runtime by the viewer's theme hook. - Modals: ``, `` — **read their CURRENT versions on `origin/main`** (redesigned in c12b3a8, newer than the analysis branch). Fixed overlays, `zIndex:1000`. - Assets: summary icons ALREADY EXIST at `public/icon-thick-{completed,investigated,learned,next-steps}.svg` (byte-equivalent artwork to `$DESIGN/mirror/assets/icon-*.svg`). Fonts go under `public/assets/fonts/` (repo convention; middleware matcher excludes `assets/`). ### Anti-patterns (repo-verified) - Do NOT read `stats.database.*` — that's the local-worker `Stats` shape; cloud payload needs the cast pattern from `useCloudData.ts:264–267`. - Do NOT name anything `useTimelineScroll` — `src/hooks/useTimelineScroll.ts` is a landing-page framer-motion hook. New ruler-sync hook = `useRailSync`, local to the viewer folder. - Do NOT put tokens on `:root` — scope to the viewer root element so nothing leaks to landing pages (old `cloud-viewer.css` put them on `:root`; it dies here). - React Compiler + `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` + `exhaustive-deps` are enforced — mirror the existing disable-comment patterns only where the old code did. - No `` without the eslint-next escape used elsewhere (`{/* eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element */}`), or use plain CSS background where cleaner. - Don't invent design values — every px/color/radius is in `DESIGN-SPEC.md`; copy, don't estimate. - Merge gate reality: **no CI, no branch protection**. `npm run lint` && `npm run build` locally + Vercel preview are the only gates — run them before merge. --- ## Phase 1 — Branch, assets, tokens, skeleton folder **Branch**: from the repo root: `git fetch origin && git switch -c viewer-timeline-cards origin/main`. Copy `$DESIGN/mirror/assets/logomark.webp` → `public/assets/cmem/logomark.webp`. 3. Icons: use the existing `/icon-thick-*.svg` in `public/` (verify visually identical to `$DESIGN/mirror/assets/icon-*.svg`; if any differ, overwrite from `$DESIGN`).

**2. Full obs cards (prompt/rail face) — the strip** (dc.html:593–676). Here each observation IS a full card (article), grouped by file. Each card DOM (e.g. 600–608):

The only prose is (a) the Learned/Completed/Next-steps summary rows, and (b) the KINDSUM distill panel text. There is no per-observation expandable body anywhere in the alt design.

**"Magic" / KINDSUM distill-by-kind** (`onMagicKind`, dc.html:2182–2189): clicking a stack's ✦ badge → `e.stopPropagation()` (so it doesn't trigger the stack's `onStackClick`), `_stopAlt('summary')` (settle + force summary face), `setState({altMagic:{kind, phase:'running'}})`, then after **1300ms** → `{kind, phase:'done'}`. The panel (dc.html:522–556) expands (`altPanelRows 1fr`) showing a spinner+label while running, then a distilled mini-summary: kind chip, `KINDSUM[kind].label` ("Discoveries, distilled" etc.), `.meta` count, a paragraph of `.text`, and cite chips from `.cites`. `KINDSUM` is fully defined at **dc.html:1455–1461** — each entry `{label, meta, chipBg, fg, text, cites:[{id, tag}]}`. Example: `discovery.cites = [{id:'obs-101258b', tag:'#101258 · history surfaced'}, {id:'obs-101259b', tag:'#101259 · data model confirmed'}]`. Cite-chip clicks call `altGoToObs(c.id)` (dc.html:2173). ## E. Contrast with the standard `#sess-s1` card (dc.html:890–1044) and §7 Live card (SPEC:663–767)

The alt card is a **stateful, animated superset** of the standard `#sess-s1` card. Structural differences an implementer must reconcile:

1. **One card renders BOTH prompt and summary faces via cross-fade; the standard card renders only the settled summary.** Standard `#sess-s1` (890) uses `order:` to stack a static prompt row (order 2, dc.html:892), butter hero (order 1, 904), and rail (order 3, 930) — all always visible. The alt card instead has a **single tinted head** whose bg (`altBg` butter⇄lilac), border, arc color, label (summary icon ⇄ "A" prompt avatar), and title (`<h2>` ⇄ `<p>`) all cross-fade on `altView`, and it **collapses the summary body and the rail in opposition** via `grid-template-rows 1fr/0fr` (2136/2139). The standard card has none of this — no `altView`, no collapse wrappers, no opacity/visibility swaps.

2. **The alt card adds three lifecycle phases in the head (`altPhase`); the standard card has none.** Streaming (Recording pill + live obs counter, 394–403), distilling (spinner pill, 404–410), and settled (Badge + Replay + Summary/Prompt segmented control, 411–422). Standard `#sess-s1` head shows only a static "Session summary" label (908–911) + time-range/Badge in the prompt row (898–901). To go from alt→standard you'd delete the entire streaming/distilling branches, the Replay button, and the segmented control.

3. **The alt card adds a by-kind observation index + distill panel that the standard card lacks.** The five `data-stack` count cards (444–521) with hover-reveal ✦ magic buttons, plus the collapsing KINDSUM distill panel (522–556) and its `altMagic` state, are entirely alt-only. The standard card jumps straight to the horizontal file-grouped strip with no aggregate index and no distill affordance.

Standard rail `s0`/`s1` are inset cards (`margin:14px 22px 20px;border-radius:16px;padding:12px 16px 10px` — dc.html:930) with a denser ruler including 10 minor ticks (944–953). Obs `data-at` fractions and the file-group/card anatomy are otherwise identical (`b`-suffixed ids being the only per-obs difference).

5. **vs the §7 Live card** (SPEC:663–767, dc.html:685): the Live card is driven by *real* SSE-style state (`live.{running,o1..o4,sum,count,tools,queue,playFrac}`, dc.html:1436) with a **moving playhead** (dc.html:783–788, `playheadStyle` 2082–2086) and a live tool-use counter + logo queue badge — none of which exist in the alt card. ## B. SessionCard.tsx — the live variant

Full file `SessionCard.tsx:1-243`. It is the parent card; ObsCard lives inside its `<Strip>`.

**Live-related state / derived state:**

  ```ts
  const [prevLive, setPrevLive] = React.useState(live);
  const [heroLanded, setHeroLanded] = React.useState(false);
  if (live !== prevLive) { setPrevLive(live); if (!live && session.hasSummary) setHeroLanded(true); }
  ```

## C. useRailSync.ts — the RailSyncApi

**Exported API** (`useRailSync.ts:46-62`, returned `:434-437`):
- `syncAll()` — re-syncs every `[data-rail]` band (`:180-184`).
- `queueSync()` — rAF-throttled syncAll (`:187-193`).
- `jumpToObs(domId)` — centers a card in its strip, scrolls its section into view, then flashes (`:210-241`).
- `jumpToSession(secId)` — smooth-scroll to a `#sess-…` section (`:196-207`).
- `landObs(domId)` — streamed-obs landing: strip-to-end + syncAll + delayed flash (`:246-268`).

**flash / highlight mechanics (what classes/attrs get toggled):**
- **Flash** is NOT a CSS class — it is an inline `element.style.animation = 'tcFlash 2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 1'` set directly on the obs `<article>` (`jumpToObs` `:232-238`; `landObs` `:258-264`), cleared to `''` after 2100 ms. The `tcFlash` keyframe is defined in CSS (viewer.css/shell.css — not cards.css). `landObs` delays the flash by 460 ms (`:257`) so it doesn't cancel the 420 ms `tcCardLand` entrance.
- **`data-hot` attribute** is the hover-affinity highlight: on `mouseover` (`_onOver`, `:333-364`) hovering a card `[data-at]` sets `data-hot="true"` on the matching `[data-dot="obs-<id>"]`, and hovering a dot sets `data-hot` on the target obs `#obs-<id>`. `_onOut` (`:367-380`) removes it. The visual styling for `[data-hot]` lives in viewer.css (dot halos), not cards.css.
- **`data-scrubbing`** attribute is set on the ruler during drag (`:293`, removed `:308`).
- **`data-band` left/width/opacity** are written inline by `syncRail` (`:124-141`).

**dot ↔ card hover/jump today:**
- Hover affinity: `_onOver`/`_onOut` toggling `data-hot` (above).
- **Click**: document-delegated `onDocClick` (`:280-284`) — `const dot = e.target.closest('[data-dot]'); if (dot) jumpToObs(dot.getAttribute('data-dot'))`. So today only **rail dots** (the `[data-dot]` buttons in Ruler.tsx) are clickable → they jump+center+flash the obs card. The obs **cards themselves** (`[data-at]`) are NOT click handlers — only hover.
- It is a single document-level delegated controller (`:271-426`), scoped to `rootRef` via the `within()` guard (`:277`), so it survives React re-renders.

**What's needed for the two new interactions the implementer wants:**
1. **"bold border highlight" on a rail obs box** — there is no border-highlight class today; only `data-hot` (dot halo) and inline `tcFlash`. Implementer can either (a) add a new attribute (e.g. `data-selected`) toggled here and a `.tcv-obscard[data-selected]` rule in cards.css, or (b) reuse the existing `data-hot` toggle path (`_onOver`/`_onOut`, `:333-380`) but extend it to write to the card and add a bold-border CSS rule. The card already receives `data-hot` on hover (`:337-338`), so a `.tcv-obscard[data-hot]` border rule is the smallest change.
2. **"click rail item → swap main card to that observation"** — today clicking a `[data-dot]` calls `jumpToObs` (scroll+flash), NOT a card swap. To swap a "main card," the click needs to reach React state (this hook is pure-DOM and holds no React state for a "selected obs"). Cleanest path: add a callback to `RailSyncCallbacks` (`:39-44`, currently only `onRailTip` + `onEscape`) like `onSelectObs(domId)`, fire it from `onDocClick` (`:280-284`) alongside/instead of `jumpToObs`, and lift a `selectedObs` state into TimelineViewer/SessionCard. There is precedent: AskCard cites already do a React-level `onClick={() => onJumpToObs(...)}` (AskCard.tsx:173) rather than going through document delegation.

input.description: Phase 1: alt chrome restructure
input.prompt:
You are the Phase 1 IMPLEMENTATION agent executing a plan. Repo: /Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro, branch `viewer-obs-card-alt` (already checked out — verify with `git branch --show-current` before editing; do NOT switch branches, do NOT commit, do NOT push, do NOT start any dev server — one is already running on port 3005 with hot reload).

FIRST: Read /Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro/PLAN-obs-card-alt.md in full — especially "Phase 0" (reference material, design essentials, mapping decisions, allowed APIs, anti-pattern guards) and "Phase 1 — Alt chrome restructure". That file is the authoritative spec; this prompt only supplements it.

Your job is Phase 1 ONLY:
1. Restructure src/components/timeline-viewer/SessionCard.tsx to the alt card's natural DOM order: section.tcv-session > div.tcv-tinthead[data-face] (arc rings + head row + title cross-fade + collapsing summary body) > rail. Delete the order: juggling and the standalone prompt row (absorb its content per the plan). Face state 'summary' | 'prompt' replaces the current view state. Copy exact style values from the plan's "Alt card design essentials" — they are copy-ready from the design source; do not invent values. Where an existing CSS class already implements a pattern (e.g. .tcv-seg segmented control, the grid-rows collapse at cards.css:134-165), reuse/adapt it rather than duplicating.
2. Head background/arc/border driven by data-face (butter-100/butter-200/transparent on summary; lilac-100/lilac-200/line-1 on prompt), 420ms transitions.
3. Wrap the rail in a grid-rows collapse pair: expanded when face !== 'summary' OR !hasSummary; collapsed on summary face. After the 480ms expand, ruler bands must re-sync — implement the onRailReveal/queueSync wiring described in plan Phase 1 step 3 (TimelineViewer holds the rail api from useRailSync; thread a callback prop).
4. Full-bleed rail chrome: .tcv-rail becomes background:var(--canvas); padding:12px 22px; margin:0; border-radius:0 (mobile: padding:10px 14px, margin:0).
5. No-summary sessions: permanent prompt face, no segmented control, rail always expanded, and the .tcv-distill placeholder no longer renders in the hero slot (leave its CSS for the Phase 5 sweep; just stop rendering it).
6. Keep the live prop rendering minimally working (live pill/eye can stay wherever they land in the head row for now — Phase 3 reworks them properly). Keep the wrap lifecycle derived-state (prevLive/heroLanded) intact. Do not touch AskCard, useCloudData, Strip/Ruler internals (except what the rail wrapper requires), or the data layer.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS (from the plan — violations fail review):
- React Compiler lint rules enforced: no setState-in-effect (use the derived-state-from-props pattern already in SessionCard.tsx:96-101); exhaustive-deps clean.
- Don't animate font-size; don't use display:none for collapses (grid-rows trick only); data-face attribute (not class toggling); no border-width changes anywhere.
- Types are VObservation/VSession from types.ts.
- The dev server auto-reloads — verify visually via curl/screenshot only if trivial; the dedicated verification agent will do the full checklist. But YOU must run: `npm run lint` (baseline: 66 pre-existing errors, ZERO errors/warnings in src/components/timeline-viewer/ files) and `npm run build` (must pass) before reporting done. If lint/build fail, fix and re-run.

REPORT BACK (mandatory evidence): files changed with a one-line summary each; the new SessionCard DOM outline; lint output tail showing baseline unchanged + zero viewer-file issues; build success line; any deviations from the plan with justification; anything you deferred.

## Phase 2 Review — Anti-Pattern + Code Quality

`const [sel, setSel] = useState(...)` lives inside `SessionCard` (SessionCard.tsx:121). Nothing lifted to TimelineViewer or a store (TimelineViewer.tsx not in diff). `useRailSync.ts` untouched. No `railApi` prop was threaded (the plan's step-3 `railApi` idea was intentionally dropped in favor of the no-double-jump model — consistent with the header comment at SessionCard.tsx:150-155).

### 3. Bold ring — CONFIRMED with one MINOR

- Card ring (cards.css:435-438): `border-color: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px var(--accent);` — color + shadow only, **no border-width change**. Correct.
- Dot ring (cards.css:441-443): `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px var(--accent), var(--shadow-card);` on `> span` — shadow only. Correct.
- Source-order claim: `.tcv-obscard:hover` is at cards.css:396, `.tcv-obscard[data-selected]` at cards.css:435. Equal specificity `(0,3,0)`, selection rule is later → wins over the card's own `:hover`. Claim holds for that path.
- data-hot rules unmodified: the hover-affinity rules live in `viewer.css:41/44/51` and are NOT in the diff. Correct.

**MINOR — SessionCard/cards.css:435 + viewer.css:51:** The in-code comment ("ring survives hover; data-hot … is separate") overstates. `viewer.css:51` — `.tcv [data-at][data-hot="true"] { border-color: var(--line-2) !important; box-shadow: var(--shadow-card) !important; … }` — uses `!important`. Obs cards carry `data-at`, so when useRailSync sets `data-hot="true"` on the *selected* card (affinity fired by hovering its matching ruler dot), this `!important` rule clobbers the accent ring's `border-color` and `box-shadow`, reverting it to the neutral hover look for the hover duration. The ring survives the card's own `:hover`, but not the `data-hot` affinity path. Transient visual glitch only; not a blocker. (The dot ring is safe — `viewer.css:44` only touches the dot span's `transform`/`outline-color`, not `box-shadow`.)

### 4. No double-jump — CONFIRMED
`grep jumpToObs|landObs|scrollInto|scrollTo|rail\.` across the 4 components returns only two **comment** lines (SessionCard.tsx:93, :155). `selectFromDot` (SessionCard.tsx:156-160) is selection-only. Obs-card clicks (`selectFromCard`, SessionCard.tsx:149-153) neither jump nor scroll, and obs cards are `id="obs-<id>"` / `.tcv-obscard` (not `[data-dot]`), so the doc-delegated `[data-dot]` handler in useRailSync:280-284 does not fire on card clicks. Cosmetic a11y inconsistency, pre-existing.

Diff touches only seeds 101258, 101260, 101261, 101263 (reformatted to multiline). All `id` / `session_id` / `project` / `type` / `title` / `file` / `read` / `at` values are byte-identical to before; only `facts[]` + `narrative` were added. **101263 has `narrative: ''`** (fixture.ts, seed 101263). **Selection state shape & handlers — sound.** `deselectTo` (SessionCard.tsx:142-147) uses a functional `setSel` with a no-op guard (`prev.obsId === null && prev.follow ? prev : …`) to skip needless re-renders. `selectFromCard` (:149-153) uses a functional toggle. `selectFromDot` (:156-160) reads `sel.obsId` from closure rather than functional form — **no stale-closure risk** because the handler is recreated every render (no `useCallback`) so `sel` is always current, and it's re-passed to the non-memoized Ruler each render. NIT: the card path uses functional update while the dot path reads closure state — harmless inconsistency, not a bug.

**narrOpen reset discipline — adequate.** Reset to `false` in all three handlers (SessionCard.tsx:144, 150, 158). NIT: the one path not covered is a *prop-driven* dangling selection (selected obs filtered out of `observations` → `selectedObs` becomes `undefined`, SessionCard.tsx:128); `narrOpen` is not reset there. Harmless — the narrative UI renders only on the obs face, and the next explicit selection resets it. No user-reachable Phase 2 path leaves a stale-open narrative visible. (Phase 3's auto-follow will need to route selection changes through a handler that also resets narrOpen — worth carrying forward, but out of scope here.)

**Duplicate DOM / shared slot — clean.** The collapsing body (SessionCard.tsx:338-395) renders exactly one of `.tcv-obsbody` or `.tcv-herorows` via a ternary (`selectedObs ? … : rows.length > 0 && …`), so there is no duplicated summary/obs content in the slot. **Memoization — non-issue.** No `React.memo` on ObsCard, Strip, or Ruler. The per-row inline callback `onSelect={onSelectObs ? () => onSelectObs(domId) : undefined}` (Strip.tsx) therefore does not defeat any memo, and `selectFromCard`/`selectFromDot` being recreated each render is fine. Informational only: if ObsCard is memoized later (e.g. for large rails), these unstable per-row callbacks plus the non-`useCallback` handlers would defeat it — would need `useCallback` + a stable per-row binding at that point.

**No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.** One MINOR (item 3: `data-hot` `!important` rule in viewer.css:51 overrides the obs-card selection ring during dot-hover affinity — the "ring survives hover" comment is only half-true). ## 2. Derived-state correctness — NO VIOLATIONS (scrutinized hard)

**a. Auto-follow block (`SessionCard.tsx:158-165`)** — correct.
- Guarded on `lastObsDomId !== prevLastObsId`; `setPrevLastObsId(lastObsDomId)` runs on every fire, so the guard is false next render → cannot loop.
- `setPrevLastObsId` is OUTSIDE the inner `if (live && sel.follow && lastObsDomId)`, so `prevLastObsId` tracks the newest id even when `live=false`/`follow=false`. No stale-prev mis-fire later. Exactly the required behavior.
- On mount, `prevLastObsId` inits to `lastObsDomId` (`:158`), so the block does NOT fire on first render — initial selection comes from the lazy `sel` initializer instead (no double-set).

**b. Wrap block (`:220-230`) vs auto-follow ordering** — no hazard.

**c. Mount initial selection (`:142-145`)** — correct.

## Aggregation code (SessionCard.tsx)
```tsx
const stacks: { type: string; count: number; firstDomId: string }[] = [];
if (session.hasSummary && observations.length > 0) {
  const byType = new Map<string, { count: number; earliest: VObservation }>();
  for (const o of observations) {
    const entry = byType.get(o.type);
    if (!entry) byType.set(o.type, { count: 1, earliest: o });
    else {
      entry.count += 1;
      if (o.at < entry.earliest.at) entry.earliest = o;
    }
  }
  const ordered = [
    ...Object.keys(TYPE_META).filter((t) => byType.has(t)),
    ...[...byType.keys()].filter((t) => !(t in TYPE_META)),
  ];
  for (const t of ordered) {
    const entry = byType.get(t);
    if (entry) stacks.push({ type: t, count: entry.count, firstDomId: `obs-${entry.earliest.id}` });
  }
}
```
Unknown types trail in first-seen order and use the same `meta?.chip ?? 'var(--canvas)'` / `meta?.fg ?? 'var(--ink-2)'` fallback ObsCard uses (no icon).

## Pending-jump code (option (a), transition-driven — no timers)
```tsx
const pendingJumpRef = React.useRef<string | null>(null);
const selectFromStack = (domId: string) => {
  setNarrOpen(false);
  setSel({ obsId: domId, follow: domId === lastObsDomId });
  if (face !== 'summary') onObsReveal?.(domId);   // already-open guard: fire immediately
  else pendingJumpRef.current = domId;
};
```
```tsx
onTransitionEnd={(e) => {
  if (e.target !== e.currentTarget || e.propertyName !== 'grid-template-rows') return;
  onRailReveal?.();
  const pending = pendingJumpRef.current;
  if (pending) {
    pendingJumpRef.current = null;
    if (railOpen) onObsReveal?.(pending);   // only fire on the EXPAND; a collapse just clears
  }
}}
```
The design's 540ms `altGoToObs` timer is replaced by the actual 480ms grid-rows transition boundary; a mid-flight deselect ends with `railOpen=false` and silently discards the stale target.

- **Phase 3 regression** (`phase3-impl-check.mjs`): **28/28 PASS** — live cycle, pin/follow, wrap, ended state, reduced-motion all intact with stacks inside the collapsing body.

## Deviations
1. **Tooltip always includes N** ("See the 1 decision card in the timeline") — the dc.html demo drops the count in the singular ("See the decision card…"), but the task spec explicitly requires "See the N <kind> card(s)" with correct plurality; followed the task spec.
2. **Dropped the demo's `opacity 200ms` from the stack transition** — it existed only for KINDSUM-panel dimming, which is omitted per plan mapping decision #5.
3. **Added `height:100%` on `.tcv-stackfront`** (not in demo) — keeps front/back layers aligned under the container's `align-items:stretch` if a label ever wraps; invisible when heights are equal.
4. **`onObsReveal` also clears the RailTip** in TimelineViewer before jumping — the clicked stack unmounts so no mouseout would ever clear its hover tip; matches the existing jumpToSession tip-clear convention.

## Phase 4 Review — Anti-Pattern + Code Quality

Scope confirmed: `git status` shows only `SessionCard.tsx`, `TimelineViewer.tsx`, `cards.css` modified. `useRailSync.ts` and `fixture.ts` are untouched. `.claude/skills/cmem-pro-architecture/` is an unrelated untracked dir (not part of this diff).

### 1. No setState-in-effect / no new useEffect / no timers — NO VIOLATIONS
The diff adds exactly one hook: `React.useRef<string | null>(null)` (SessionCard.tsx:241). No `useEffect`, no `setTimeout`, no `setInterval` introduced. The pre-existing module-level clock `setInterval` (SessionCard.tsx:100-103) is untouched context. The pending jump is purely ref + `onTransitionEnd` driven (SessionCard.tsx:596-607). `setState` calls in `selectFromStack` (`setNarrOpen`, `setSel`, 243-244) are in an event handler, not render/effect. The `stacks` aggregation (293-312) is pure render, no setState. Clean.

### 2. Pending-jump ref correctness

**(2b) deselect mid-expand → discard — CORRECT, NO VIOLATION.** The `onTransitionEnd` is an inline arrow in JSX (SessionCard.tsx:596), recreated every render, so its closure captures the *current* render's `railOpen` (derived `face !== 'summary'`, line 319). If the user deselects mid-expand, the expand transition is cancelled (fires `transitioncancel`, not `transitionend`) and a reverse collapse runs; the collapse's `transitionend` executes against the latest render where `face==='summary'` → `railOpen===false` → the `if (railOpen)` guard at line 605 discards the parked target. Stale jump correctly avoided.

**(2c) already-selected-obs immediate-fire — NO double-jump, path is unreachable.** Stacks render only in the non-`selectedObs` branch of the body (SessionCard.tsx:513-582), so they do **not** exist in the DOM on the obs face — you cannot click a stack while an obs is selected. The `if (face !== 'summary') onObsReveal?.(domId)` immediate branch (line 245) is reachable only on the prompt face, but on the prompt face the herobody is `visibility:hidden` (cards.css:151-156, `data-face="prompt"` not in the visible selector at 158-159), so the stacks are non-interactive there too. The immediate-fire branch is therefore effectively defensive; no double-jump can occur because `railOpen` doesn't change when firing immediately (no grid-rows transition → no second `transitionend`). No violation.

**(2d) transitionend cross-talk — NO VIOLATION.** The guard `if (e.target !== e.currentTarget || e.propertyName !== 'grid-template-rows') return` (SessionCard.tsx:597) restricts firing to the railwrap's own grid-rows transition. The herobody collapse (`.tcv-herobodywrap`, cards.css:144-150) also animates `grid-template-rows`, but it lives inside `.tcv-tinthead`, a *sibling* of `.tcv-railwrap` — not a descendant — so its `transitionend` never bubbles to this handler. The `narrwrap` collapse is likewise inside the tinthead. No cross-talk.

**(2a) FINDING — MINOR: stack-then-rail-card stale jump.** SessionCard.tsx:602-606 + 216-230. Two *stack* clicks can't race (stacks unmount once `face==='obs'`). But `pendingJumpRef` is only ever cleared/overwritten by `selectFromStack`; `selectFromCard` (216) and `selectFromDot` (225) do not touch it. Sequence: click stack A on the summary face → `pendingJumpRef='obs-A'`, rail begins its 480ms expand → user clicks obs **card B** in the rail before the expand completes (cards become clickable in the final portion of the grow) → `sel` moves to B but the ref still holds A → expand `transitionend` fires with `railOpen===true` → `onObsReveal('obs-A')` centers+flashes A while the ring sits on B. Cosmetic (selection ring is correct; only the center/flash targets the wrong obs) and a narrow timing window, hence MINOR. A one-line clear of `pendingJumpRef.current = null` inside `selectFromCard`/`selectFromDot` would close it.

### 3. Aggregation
- **Key order — correct.** `Object.keys(TYPE_META).filter((t) => byType.has(t))` (SessionCard.tsx:305) preserves TYPE_META insertion order (discovery, decision, feature, refactor, bugfix, …).
- **Unknowns trailing, first-seen order — correct.** `[...byType.keys()].filter((t) => !(t in TYPE_META))` (306); the Map preserves observation-iteration insertion order = first-seen. Matches the plan's "trailing in first-seen order."
- **Earliest-by-`at` — correct.** `if (o.at < entry.earliest.at) entry.earliest = o` (301) selects min `at`, not first-in-array; `firstDomId = obs-${entry.earliest.id}` (310).
- **Fallback colors — EXACT match to ObsCard.** Stack chip uses `meta?.chip ?? 'var(--canvas)'` / `meta?.fg ?? 'var(--ink-2)'` (SessionCard.tsx:561-562, 567), byte-identical to ObsCard.tsx:53,57. (Ruler's dot fallback is `?? 'var(--ink-3)'`, but that governs the dot fill, not the chip; the plan says "the same fallback colors ObsCard uses" — matched.)
- **No premature memoization — correct.** `stacks` is a plain per-render const (293-312), gated by `session.hasSummary && observations.length > 0`. No `useMemo` with wrong deps.
- **FINDING — NIT: `in` operator prototype footgun.** SessionCard.tsx:306 (`!(t in TYPE_META)`) and 305/537 (`TYPE_META[type]`). Because `in` walks the prototype chain, an observation `type` colliding with an `Object.prototype` name (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf`) would be excluded from *both* the known list (not an own key of TYPE_META) *and* the unknown list (`t in TYPE_META` is true via inheritance), silently dropping that stack. Real observation types are a controlled semantic set (discovery/decision/feature/…), so this is unreachable with production data — NIT. `Object.hasOwn(TYPE_META, t)` would be the robust form. The `byType` Map itself is safe for any key.

### 4. CSS vs the plan's copy-ready block — NO VIOLATIONS
Verified against cards.css:178-227:
- container (`.tcv-stacks`): `flex; align-items:stretch; gap:12px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-top:16px; padding-top:6px` ✓
- stack (`.tcv-stack`): `width:134px; flex:none; position:relative; cursor:pointer; transition:transform 140ms var(--ease-out)`, hover `translateY(-2px)` ✓
- front (`.tcv-stackfront`): `flex column; gap:7px; padding:10px 11px; border-radius:12px; box-shadow:var(--shadow-card); background:var(--paper); border:1px solid var(--line-1)` ✓ (plus `height:100%`/`position:relative` supporting `align-items:stretch` — benign additions)
- head chip: reuses `.tcv-obschip` = 22×22 r8 (cards.css:454-461) + icon `size={13}` (SessionCard.tsx:565) + label `.tcv-obstype` 11px/500 (cards.css:462) ✓
- count: `.tcv-stackcount b` 16px/700 (219-224), unit `span` 10.5px `--ink-meta` (225) ✓
- back layer (`.tcv-stackback`): `position:absolute; inset:0; transform:translate(4px,-4px); background:var(--paper); border:1px solid var(--line-1); border-radius:12px; opacity:0.6; pointer-events:none` ✓ exact

- No `magic`/`KINDSUM` CSS anywhere. ✓

### 5. Tooltip / pos / RailTip clear — NO VIOLATIONS
- Pluralization: `card${count === 1 ? '' : 's'}` in both the tip (SessionCard.tsx:545) and the count unit (573). ✓
- `data-tip-pos="above"` (546) matches the ruler-dot convention (Ruler.tsx:79) and is read by `useRailSync.ts:350` / `RailTip.tsx:27`. The stacks sit inside `.tcv` (rootRef target, TimelineViewer.tsx:306), so `within()` (useRailSync.ts:277) passes and the hover tooltip fires.
- `onObsReveal` clears the tip first: `setRailTip(null); rail.jumpToObs(domId)` (TimelineViewer.tsx:379-381) — identical to the `jumpToSession` convention at TimelineViewer.tsx:281-283. ✓

### 6. Prop typing / optionality / wiring — NO VIOLATIONS
- `onObsReveal?: (domId: string) => void` (SessionCard.tsx:135) — optional, correctly typed to `domId: string`.
- Graceful degradation: every call site uses optional chaining (`onObsReveal?.(...)` at 245 and 605). The only other `TimelineViewerView` mounts (viewer-preview page.tsx:125/144/145) render through TimelineViewer, whose sole `SessionCard` call site now passes `onObsReveal` (TimelineViewer.tsx:379). Absent-prop path is safe regardless.
- Wiring stability: `SessionCard` is a plain function (not `React.memo`), so the inline `onObsReveal` arrow being recreated each render costs nothing extra — the card re-renders with its parent anyway. NIT only: `onRailReveal={rail.queueSync}` is a stable `useCallback` while `onObsReveal` is an inline arrow; harmless given no memoization, but inconsistent in style.

### 7. A11y — NO BLOCKERS (one NIT)
- `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}`, `onKeyDown` for `Enter`/`' '` with `e.preventDefault()` (SessionCard.tsx:542-553). `preventDefault` on Space correctly suppresses page scroll; on Enter it's harmless. ✓
- **NIT:** no explicit `aria-label` on the stack. The accessible name falls back to text content → "discovery 3 cards" (the chip icon is an empty decorative `<span>`). That is meaningful, so no BLOCKER, but it drops the richer context the visible tooltip carries ("See the 3 discovery cards in the timeline"). Adding `aria-label={data-tip text}` would make the button self-describing for AT users, who don't receive the mouse-only RailTip. Consistent with the app's mouse-only tooltip pattern otherwise.

### 8. eslint-disable / `any` / untouched files — NO VIOLATIONS
- Only two `eslint-disable` comments in SessionCard.tsx (lines 324, 519) — both pre-existing `@next/next/no-img-element` escapes; line 519 was merely re-indented into the new fragment, not added. No new disables.
- No `any`, no type assertions to `any` in the diff.
- `useRailSync.ts` and `fixture.ts` are not in `git status` — untouched. ✓

### 9. Regression risk — NO VIOLATIONS
- **Phase 1 `queueSync` unchanged:** the railwrap `onTransitionEnd` guard was inverted from `if (match) onRailReveal()` to `if (!match) return; onRailReveal(); …` (SessionCard.tsx:597-598) — behaviorally identical for `onRailReveal`, which still fires unconditionally on every completed grid-rows transition before the pending-jump block. Phase 1 rail re-measure is intact.
- **Summary body collapses with taller stacks:** `.tcv-herobodyclip` uses `min-height:0; overflow:hidden` with the `grid-template-rows: 0fr` trick (cards.css:144-156) — no `max-height`, so arbitrary-height stack content collapses to zero cleanly on the prompt/live faces. No broken overflow assumption.

### Code quality
- **Stacks JSX (SessionCard.tsx:534-580):** a clean `stacks.map`, but ~45 lines of inline nesting (chip → icon → label → count). Readable, though extracting a small `StackCard` subcomponent would trim the render body. NIT.
- **Ordered-types construction (304-307):** clean and idiomatic (known-in-order spread + unknown trailing). Good.
- **`selectFromStack` vs `selectFromCard`/`selectFromDot` (216-247):** all three repeat the `{ obsId, follow: domId === lastObsDomId }` selection shape plus `setNarrOpen(false)`. The semantics differ (card toggles-off, dot guards on change, stack parks the jump), so full sharing isn't warranted, but the `follow` expression is duplicated three times and would benefit from a tiny `selectObs(domId)` helper returning that object. input.command:
gh pr create --title "Alt card as the observation card + fresh live animation cycle" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What this is

Rebuilds the timeline-viewer session card on the **alt card** design (`sess-s1-alt`, DESIGN-SPEC §6) — the richer lifecycle variant of the two card designs in the Timeline Cards source — and gives live sessions a fresh animation cycle centered on watching observations land in real time.

## The new cycle

1. **Session starts** → the prompt lands full-size in the lilac tinted head with a Recording pill.
2. **First observation streams in** → the prompt shrinks to a small row and the observation's title takes over the main card; its box in the rail gets a bold accent ring.
3. **Clicking any rail item** (obs card or ruler dot) swaps the main card to that observation — the primary live-viewing interaction. Landings auto-follow the newest obs; clicking an older one pins it (landings stop stealing); clicking the newest resumes following.
4. **Facts and narrative** are expandable right on the main card (grid-rows collapse, no timers).
5. **Wrap** → selection clears and the butter summary face lands, now with per-type observation stacks (click-through selects the type's earliest obs and center-flashes it after the rail expands).
6. **Summary never arrives** → the card terminates cleanly on the obs/prompt face with a time-range + count badge — the dashed "Summary distills…" placeholder is retired.

## Deliberate divergences from the design demo

- Clicking rail items swaps the **main card** to that observation (the demo's `altGoToObs` did the reverse — flipped to the rail). User-directed.
- New third face (`obs`) with facts/narrative — the design had no facts/narrative display anywhere; styled in the design language.
- Omitted demo-only elements: "alt layout" tag, Replay button, ✦ magic buttons + KINDSUM distill panel (hardcoded demo content with no production data source). Type stacks themselves are kept (pure aggregation of real observations).
- The distilling pill (post-live, pre-summary) is implemented per design but currently unreachable through the `isLiveSession` heuristic (its 30-min live window outlasts the 5-min distill window); it lights up once a real SSE wrap signal replaces the heuristic.

## Implementation notes

- Single `.tcv-tinthead[data-face="summary"|"prompt"|"obs"]` in natural DOM order; rail is full-bleed and collapses on the summary face (stacks are the index there).
- All live-cycle state is render-derived from props + the shared 20s clock — zero timers, zero effects in SessionCard; React Compiler lint stays at the repo baseline (66 pre-existing, none in viewer files).
- Selection is per-SessionCard local state; the stack click-through's center+flash jump fires from the actual 480ms grid-rows `transitionend` (no magic 540ms timer), with stale-target discard on any competing interaction.
- Data layer untouched; ask card untouched.
- Preview harness gains `?demo=ended` (settled-no-summary) alongside `?demo=live` / `?ask=1`.

## Verification

Five independent Playwright suites against the dev preview harness (fixture + `?demo=live` + `?demo=ended` + `?ask=1`): face toggles/tints/collapse choreography, full selection matrix + keyboard, the complete 20s live cycle with measured landings (±12ms of spec) including pin/resume and wrap, stacks (counts, back layers, delayed jump, 19ms rapid-toggle race), 4 themes, mobile 390px, zero console errors throughout. Per-phase anti-pattern reviews + a final pre-ship QA audit: PASS. `npm run lint` at baseline, `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_0175gu1h5jbW2kHDARtg6gd4
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

**Done. PR #46 is open with a green Vercel preview: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem-pro/pull/46** — ready for you to eyeball and merge. Screenshots of the final result are attached above.

## What was built

The alt card (the lifecycle variant from the design source, `sess-s1-alt` / DESIGN-SPEC §6) is now the session card, and your fresh animation cycle is exactly as described:

- **Session starts** → prompt and box land full-size (lilac tinted head, Recording pill).
- **First observation arrives** → the prompt shrinks to a small row and the observation's title becomes the main card; its box in the rail gets a bold accent ring.
- **Click any timeline item** (obs card or ruler dot) → the main card swaps to that observation. While live, landings auto-follow the newest obs; clicking an older one pins it, clicking the newest resumes following.
- **Facts and narrative** expand right on the main card.
- **No summary ever arrives** → the card settles cleanly on the observation view with a time-range + count badge — the dashed "Summary distills…" placeholder is gone.
- Wrapped sessions get the butter summary face with per-type observation stacks (click-through jumps to that type's earliest obs).

## Deliberate calls you should know about

- I inverted the demo's `altGoToObs` (which flipped to the rail) — clicking timeline items swaps the **main card** instead, per your description. The obs face with facts/narrative is new (the design had no facts/narrative display anywhere), styled in the design language.
- Omitted as demo-only: the "alt layout" tag, the Replay button, and the ✦ magic/KINDSUM distill panel (its content was hardcoded demo text with no production data source). The type stacks stayed — they're pure aggregation of real observations.
- The "distilling…" pill exists but won't show in production yet: the `isLiveSession` heuristic keeps sessions "live" for 30 minutes, which outlasts the 5-minute distill window. It lights up once a real SSE wrap signal replaces the heuristic.

## How it was verified

Ran as /make-plan → /do with per-phase subagents: each of the 5 phases passed an independent Playwright verification (face toggles, full selection matrix, the complete 20-second live cycle with landings measured within ±12ms, pin/resume, a 19ms rapid-toggle race on the stack jump, 4 themes, mobile) plus an anti-pattern review, and the branch cleared a final pre-ship QA audit. Lint stayed at the repo baseline (zero findings in viewer files), `tsc` and `npm run build` green throughout. The plan lives in `PLAN-obs-card-alt.md` and the design sources are preserved in `design/timeline-cards/` — both git-excluded from the PR.

One follow-up worth considering later: ask-card citation jumps still use the old scroll+flash path, so a citation into a summary-faced session flashes a card inside the collapsed rail — routing citations through selection (like stacks do) would be a nice small enhancement.
